text: Three international exhibitions bring lifestyle industries together

HCM CITY - Three international trade exhibitions featuring lingerie, mother and baby products, and home textiles opened at the Saigon Exhibition and Convention Centre in HCM City on November 19, bringing together manufacturers, suppliers, and buyers to explore business opportunities.
Organised by Informa Markets Vietnam, SIUF Vietnam, CBME Vietnam, and HOMETEX Vietnam feature more than 200 brands and companies.
Vietnam Intimate Fashion & Sourcing Expo builds on the success of SIUF Shenzhen, one of the world's largest exhibitions for the industry.

CBME Vietnam, the International Vietnam Children, Baby and Maternity Industry Expo, returns for its second edition, while HOMETEX Vietnam makes its debut as a sourcing platform for window and wall coverings, home textiles, and interior decoration.
Ben Wong, country manager of Informa Markets Vietnam, said bringing the three under one roof is an important milestone.

The exhibitions reflected interconnected consumer needs, from intimate apparel and children's products to home furnishings, with common priorities including materials, design, safety and quality standards, he said.

With a population of over 100 million, a fast-growing middle class and the rapid rise of modern retail and e-commerce, Việt Nam is not only a manufacturing base for global brands, but also a market where Vietnamese brands are growing in confidence and ambition, he said.

"This is the moment to move from 'Made in Vietnam' to 'Brands of Vietnam'," he said, emphasising the role of international trade platforms in connecting global suppliers with Vietnamese businesses and fostering long-term partnerships.
The three-day programme features product displays, fashion shows, industry seminars, and business matching.
Buyer delegations from Cambodia and Malaysia are expected to take part in around 50 pre-arranged meetings focusing on sourcing, manufacturing capabilities, and regional cooperation.
At SIUF Vietnam, fashion shows featuring Ninh Khương, MAYA, and Ben&Todd showcased a range of designs and products.

A seminar titled "From 'Made in Vietnam' to 'Brand of Vietnam': Technology, Supply Chains and Vietnamese Lingerie Brands" explored opportunities for local manufacturers to develop their own brands and become more competitive.

Speaking at the opening ceremony, Lê Văn Danh, deputy director of the HCM City Department of Industry and Trade, said the three exhibitions catered to everyday consumer needs and would help strengthen links across the value chain, from materials and design to manufacturing and distribution.

He said the city is running its usual year-end consumer stimulus programme and preparing for the 2027 Lunar New Year under the "Vibrant Ho Chi Minh City" initiative, which seeks to develop an integrated shopping, consumption, and service ecosystem in 2026-30.

He urged organisers and participating businesses to link the exhibitions with the city's programme through practical promotions, cashless payments, and digital platforms, and ensure product quality and safety, particularly for children's products, transparency about origins, and respect for intellectual property rights.
The department would support businesses through trade promotion and consumer stimulus activities, he added.
The exhibitions run until November 21. - VNS
